Scope of record: docs/plans/OPERATING-PLAN-2026-09-21.md. Manager contract: .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md.
The previous 323-row file is preserved verbatim at
RULES FOR THIS FILE, because the last one grew 67 top-level keys and 323 rows:
1. items[] is the content. Top-level keys are schema only - no narrative,
no timestamped manager_observation_* / manager_tick_* entries, no incident logs.
Three observations an hour apart on one row is the failure mode, not diligence.
2. ONE status field: `state`, from the `states` vocabulary below. There is no `status`.
3. `done` and `landed_unproven` are DIFFERENT FACTS and are never collapsed.
4. A row that is neither a plan item nor a live lane does not belong here.
A question goes to research/queue/<id>.yaml instead.
5. This file is served to the operator as the live Workflow page via
GET /api/bot/work/checklist, read from the VM's working tree. ict-git-sync
pulls main every ~5 min, so the page is as fresh as the last push TO MAIN.
cycle_intent: Make the promotion ladder mechanical and the research loop terminate in a decision. Edge is decided offline; a book only ever checks mechanics and cost.

states.queued: scoped and agreed, nobody started it
states.in_flight: a lane is actively working it
states.blocked: waiting on the typed edge(s) in blocked_on
states.dropped: deliberately not doing; note says why

item_schema.id: plan item id (A1..D3) or a lane id
item_schema.title: one line
item_schema.lane: session id once dispatched, else null
item_schema.model: the model chosen for the lane, with the reason in `note`
item_schema.ceiling_usd: per-lane dollar ceiling; on breach READ what it produced, then kill or re-scope
item_schema.spend_usd: actual, filled in by the cost meter (A1)
item_schema.tier: 1 | 2 | 3 - the approval the resulting change needs
item_schema.blocked_on: typed edges [{kind, ref, what}] — kind is `work_item` or `operator_decision`, ref names the blocker, what says why. Empty list = nothing declared blocks it.
item_schema.note: what is true about this row. Not a log.

items.title: Cost meter — usage against the WEEKLY PLAN ALLOWANCE, plus per-lane dollars
items.note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-21: 'pace ourselves based on the weekly budget for the $200 Max plan -- 10% of the weekly budget a day, so we leave a wide margin for error or unexpected needs.' 10%/day x 7 = 70% of the weekly allowance, 30% margin. [!] THIS CHANGES WHAT THIS ITEM MEASURES AND THE CHANGE IS NOT COSMETIC. A subscription plan's constraint is a WEEKLY USAGE ALLOWANCE, not a dollar spend. Every cost_usd figure in the plan (the $125 across two resumed lanes, the $11.88 in ten minutes) is API-EQUIVALENT PRICING read off session metadata -- the right signal for COMPARING lanes, the wrong denominator for PACING against a plan. Report usage-against-allowance as the budget line, keep dollars beside it as the per-lane comparison. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND MUST NOT BE INVENTED: the exact weekly allowance is not readable from this repo. FIRST JOB is to establish it from whatever surface reports plan usage, or from the operator, and to report `unknown` rather than substitute a figure until it has. A fabricated denominator under a real rule is worse than no meter.

items.title: Pull the two negative-OOS legs off alpaca_live
items.note: tlt_pullback_1h (-4.41R, n=94) and tlt_pullback_1d (-3.92R, n=8, 0 of 4 folds positive). One-line config change, reversible, does NOT wait on D1. TIER-3. APPROVED BY THE OPERATOR 2026-09-21 in conversation, verbatim: 'yeah, you can pull those strategies off if they need to be turned off.' Shipped as its own PR rather than inside the reset diff -- the one line that touches real money should not be reviewed inside a 360-file Tier-1 refactor. [!] THIS DOES NOT RETIRE THE QUESTION THE 1h LEG WAS ASKING. Its purpose was to prove real fills reconcile against exchange truth on a CASH book, and it never answered: ZERO long signals ever reached this account (18x Jun / 2x Jul / 13x Aug / 0x Sep, going quiet the day before the account was armed), and every package since 08-31 was SHORT, unexecutable here because the venue reads shorting_enabled: false. The alpaca_live order path is therefore STILL UNEXERCISED after this change. The three surviving legs inherit that job, and nothing yet checks that they do it -- if they also go quiet, the account is armed and proving nothing. [!] ROSTER-SYNC IS UNAFFECTED and this was verified, not assumed: the invariant is a SUBSET assertion (test_alpaca_portfolio_mirrors_alpaca_live_minus_proxies), so shrinking the live roster can never break it. Both legs stay in alpaca_portfolio, where their paper record keeps accruing. [!] MEASURED WHILE SHIPPING THIS, and it is the sharper version of the asymmetry finding: scripts/check_dry_run_in_diff.py reports 'dry_run_in_diff: clean' on THIS diff. Removing a leg from a roster is NOT guarded -- only the literal mode:/execution: fields are. Two spellings of 'off', one guarded. B1 must key on ROSTER MEMBERSHIP.

THIS IS THE UNSOLVED PROBLEM THE RESET HAS SO FAR ONLY RELOCATED: archiving the registers removed where work rotted and did not build what pulls it through, so until this lands follow-through is WORSE than before -- the rows are in git history and nothing reads them. Design: plan section 3b. The pull is a scheduled render into the brief's section 0 plus a required same-day disposition, NOT a guard. The forcing function is that an unrouted due item appears on the OPERATOR'S page every day until routed, and the unrouted count is a number in section 5 -- which is the one structural difference from DUE.md, whose due-list was read by machinery that was read by nobody.

items.title: Invert the execution-gate guard — evidence required to reach a Stage-2 roster
items.note: THE LOAD-BEARING CHANGE. Today check_dry_run_in_diff.py blocks turning a leg OFF and nothing blocks turning one ON; across 78 guards there is no counterpart. Demotion becomes free; promotion to a real-money roster requires a fresh evidence record clearing its declared bar. Tier-2 (CI + order-path policy) and needs the operator on the bar definition. [!] REFINED 2026-09-21 BY RUNNING THE GUARD, not by reading it: check_dry_run_in_diff.py matches ADDED `mode: dry_run` / `execution: shadow` LINES, so there are TWO spellings of 'off' and it sees only one. Removing a leg from an account's strategies: roster is NOT guarded -- verified against the A6 diff, which removes two legs from alpaca_live and reports `clean`. SO B1 MUST KEY ON ROSTER MEMBERSHIP, not on the mode/execution fields: a guard watching only the fields can be walked around by editing the list, in either direction. This also matters for the mandates -- MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 adds a leg to a roster, which is exactly the edit the current guard cannot see.

items.title: Decide what the Alpaca mirror is FOR, then make its invariant say that
items.note: RE-SCOPED 2026-09-21, same day it was written. The first version said 'extend the Bybit roster-sync test to alpaca_live / alpaca_portfolio' on the premise that NO invariant existed. THAT PREMISE WAS FALSE and was inferred rather than checked (a RULE ONE failure). tests/test_paper_portfolio_accounts.py::test_alpaca_portfolio_mirrors_alpaca_live_minus_proxies DOES exist and asserts set(live legs minus affordability proxies) <= set(portfolio legs), in every state. What is true and still a problem: that is a SUBSET assertion, deliberately, so it protects real money (no live leg without a paper counterpart) and does NOT make the mirror representative. Measured 2026-09-21: live 5 legs, mirror 14 -- nine mirror legs are not on the live book -- so Gate 2's demotion signal cannot be read off the mirror's aggregate. The test's own comment argues that asserting equality during a staged go-live would force alpaca_portfolio from 14 legs to 1 and destroy the paper research book. That argument is good and must be ANSWERED, not overwritten.

items.title: The mandate mechanism — arm the fully-automated ladder

blocked_on.what: The evidence guard is what makes the three-clause bar checkable rather than asserted.

items.note: OPERATOR GRANT 2026-09-21, verbatim: 'All the ladder decisions can be automated -- that is a standing mandate. Strategies can be promoted to live money without explicit operator approval if the evidence supports the decision. I should just get a ping in realtime of the update and an evidence review in the next daily briefing.' FIVE MANDATES ARE GRANTED: MD-PROMOTE-S0-S1, MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 (REAL MONEY), MD-DEMOTE-S2-S1, MD-DEMOTE-S1-OFF, MD-KILL-QUESTION. Build config/mandates.yaml + the resolver + the ping + the section-1 evidence render. [!] THE FILE IS NOT CREATED AHEAD OF THE RESOLVER -- a config nothing reads is the 'declared capability with no consumer' antipattern this repo already names. [!] WHAT CARRIES THE SAFETY IS 'if the evidence supports it': a COMMITTED evidence record, named harness, stated n, net of the FULL cost stack, clearing a rule registered before the run. A claim in a PR body is not a record; B1 is what makes that checkable. [!] MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 MUST NOT ARM UNTIL D1 LANDS -- arithmetic, not caution: the harnesses default slippage and funding to 0.0, so every 'passed the backtest' verdict in today's corpus is fee-only and optimistic by an unknown amount (+0.57R on the one leg measured). The derisk_only mandates carry no such block; they read live measurement, not the corpus. Bounds and the bar's content are operator decisions -- plan open decisions 5 and 6. [!] THE BAR AND THE CAP ARE NOW DECIDED (2026-09-21), so B5 builds against fixed numbers rather than waiting on them. BAR, all three clauses: expectancy > 0 net of the FULL cost stack at n >= 30 closed; positive in a MAJORITY of walk-forward folds; Stage-1 realized cost within a stated tolerance of modelled cost. CAP: total declared risk across AUTO-PROMOTED legs <= 25% of the account's configured risk budget, and NO RATE LIMIT -- a leg-per-week cap was offered and declined, so a batch CAN land in one day and the 25% number is load-bearing on its own. The cap counts auto-promoted legs ONLY; a leg the operator placed by hand does not consume the mandate's budget.

items.note: Asked explicitly rather than assumed. Lifetime real-money expectancy is -0.3231R over n=431. If R1 demotes most of the fleet the live books may be near-empty for a period. items.note: THE SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE ENGINEERING ITEM: R1 depends on it and R1 gates everything, including the arming of MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2. execution_costs.py is correct; the defect is at the call sites -- harness globals set SLIPPAGE_BPS_ROUNDTRIP and FUNDING_BPS_PER_WINDOW to 0.0, documented as deliberate for backward compatibility. THAT ARGUMENT HAS EXPIRED: it preserved comparability with runs we no longer trust. 6 of 15 harnesses carry no cost terms at all, including vwap. [!] KEEP resolve_cost_policy's None-vs-explicit-0.0 distinction: a fee-only ARM is a legitimate experiment, a fee-only DEFAULT is the defect.

items.title: A real corpus, and one way to get candles
items.note: The default fixture is 5,001 rows spanning 3.5 days of 2022; anything falling back to it produces a confident answer about nothing. Per-symbol committed corpus with stated coverage, --data made mandatory, a guard failing a run whose input row count is below a floor. [!] THE FIXTURE STAYS -- it is the fast smoke path and deleting it breaks every self-test. What changes is that reaching it BY DEFAULT becomes impossible.

items.title: Every research workflow lands a durable queryable result
items.note: 19 of 23 produce an artifact and an issue comment: artifacts expire, comments are not queryable. This is what makes MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 POSSIBLE AT ALL -- without it there is no evidence record for the mandate to read. One result schema, one committed location, the commit step in the shared composite action rather than re-implemented 19 times.

items.title: Unblock replay-pregate
items.note: TWO independent faults and both must go: runtime_logs/** is not in TIER1_SURFACE so pr-landing R5 rejects the commit (0 reports on main since inception), AND the trainer swap-thrashes so 6 of 6 runs die at 10 of 22 heads with NO non-BTC head ever graded. [!] Fixing only the surface produces a green workflow that still grades a third of the fleet -- do not report it fixed on the commit landing. Raising trainer memory is an OCI capacity question: the Ampere pool is FULL at 4 of 4 OCPU.

items.title: Wire the 9 orphan backtest harnesses
items.note: A harness with no workflow runs when a human remembers it, which is never. One dispatchable workflow per family, taking leg + corpus as inputs, landing through E5. A queued research unit names its instrument, and the instrument must be dispatchable for the queue to mean anything.

Capacity is NOT the constraint; results not becoming decisions is, and E3-E7 fix that. Idle capacity that exists: GitHub-hosted runners, free for this repo.
